generatedNotes: Legends re-tiers the whole Ranger book downward. In classic (P99) Rangers get their first spells at 9 and level in blocks (9/15/22/30/39/49/50+); on Legends the same spells appear from level 1 upward with per-level granularity. Level differences between `members[].level` (Legends, authoritative) and the classic level noted in `note` are therefore expected and systematic, not per-spell errors.

Legends also re-scales magnitudes: heals, DoTs and DD are markedly stronger than classic (e.g. Healing 135-175 vs classic 84-100; Stinging Swarm 27-42/tick vs classic 13/tick; Immolate 42-67/tick vs classic 24/tick), while AC on the coat line is slightly lower than classic.

Observed data-shape tell in the input file: effect strings phrased 'Increase Armor Class by N' carry Legends-tuned (usually lower) AC, while 'Increase AC by N' rows reproduce the classic P99 numbers verbatim. Every Skin-line spell appears TWICE in the file, once in each phrasing. See skin-line notes and openQuestions.

Stacking model used throughout: P99 Buff Lines groups every buff by the effect slot it writes to. 'Buffs under the same heading can't be stacked together.' Cross-line conflicts below are derived from shared headings/slots on that page.

members.name: Skin Like Nature

members.name: Skin Like Nature
members.note: Classic row: Druid 49 / Ranger 59, AC 16, max HP 248-250, +2 HP/tick. Top of the Ranger chain.

replacement.note: Later members overwrite earlier ones (all write AC slot 1 and the HP Primary 'AC and HP' column, so only one can be up). BUT the chain is not monotonic in HP: Skin Like Rock scales to 105 max HP at L65 while Skin Like Steel caps at 100 max HP at L50. Above ~L50 a Ranger trades 5 max HP for 3-4 AC by moving from Rock to Steel. This quirk is classic and Legends reproduces it verbatim in both rows. Skin Like Diamond (200 HP) and Nature (250 HP) are unambiguous upgrades.

conflicts.detail: Courage, Center, Daring, Bravery, Valor, Resolution, Heroism and Fortitude all sit in AC slot 1 and in the same HP-Primary 'AC and HP' column as the Skin line. A cleric's Valor/Resolution/Heroism overwrites Skin Like Diamond/Nature and vice versa - only one lands.

Aegolism (Cleric 60) is the AC slot 1 & 4 combination buff: it blocks the Skin line AND the Aegis line at once. Per the page's own rule, a combination buff does not stack with the buffs listed underneath it.
Protection of the Glades (Druid 60, +24 AC / +470 HP) is the top of the same AC slot 1 / HP-Primary column. It overwrites any Skin-line buff on the Ranger.
Natureskin (Druid 57, +19 AC / +400 HP / +4 regen) is the Druid-only successor in the same slot; it replaces Skin Like Nature and also collides with Skin Like Nature's +2 regen in HP-Regen slot 4.
Inner Fire (Shaman 1, +3 AC / +20 HP) is in AC slot 1 - same line, blocked by any Skin buff.
Armor of Protection (Cleric 34) appears in the HP-Primary 'AC and HP' column (+225 HP), so it collides with the Skin line on HP even though its AC lives in slot 2.

Only for Skin Like Nature: its +2 HP/tick is HP-Regeneration slot 4, shared with Natureskin (+4) and the Rejuvenation potions (+10/+20/+40). A Rejuvenation potion will block or be blocked by Skin Like Nature's regen component.

stacksWith.detail: The Cleric Symbol line (Transal -> Ryltan -> Pinzarn -> Naltron -> Marzin, plus Naltron's Mark) is the separate 'HP Only and Requires Gem' column of HP (Primary). Per the page's column rule the two columns stack: Skin Like Nature + Symbol of Marzin both land. This is the standard Ranger buff pairing. Note the shared blocker: Aegolism combines both columns and therefore blocks both.
Cleric Holy Armor -> Guard -> Armor of Faith -> Shield of Words -> Aegis (and Bulwark of Faith) are AC slot 4; the Skin line is AC slot 1. They stack. Only Aegolism (slot 1 & 4) breaks this.

Shaman Talisman of Tnarg/Altuna/Kragg and the caster Shielding line are the separate 'HP (Shielding / Talisman)' heading; they stack with Skin-line HP. Focus of Spirit (Shaman 60) is explicitly exempted from the combination-blocking rule on that page.
Thistlecoat/Barbcoat/Bramblecoat/Spikecoat/Thorncoat are AC slot 2 - stack with the Skin line.
Riftwind's Protection / Call of Earth are AC slot 3 - stack with the Skin line.
Strength of Nature's +75 max HP is the 'HP (Strength)' heading, separate from HP (Primary) - it stacks with Skin-line HP. See the caveat in atk-self-line about its stacking block.

stacking.notes: The Ranger's ceiling stack is Skin Like Nature (AC1/HP) + Symbol of Marzin (HP) + Aegis/Bulwark (AC4) + a coat (AC2) + Call of Earth (AC3) + a Talisman/Shielding (HP). Accepting a cleric Heroism or an Aegolism replaces the Skin buff rather than adding to it.

CRITICAL: Strength of Nature carries an explicit stacking block - 'Block new spell if slot 4 is effect Max Hitpoints and < 400'. While it is up, incoming buffs whose slot 4 is a max-HP increase below 400 are refused. That covers Skin Like Nature (250), Skin Like Diamond (200), Valor (200), Resolution (250) and the lower Symbols. Cast the HP buffs FIRST, then Strength of Nature. The same effect text appears verbatim in the Legends file and on P99, so this is classic behaviour Legends inherits.

members.note: Classic Druid 44 / Ranger 59. P99 notes it is poor value vs casting Firestrike twice - Legends keeps the same shape (450 for 250 mana vs 422 for 155).

replacement.note: Straight damage upgrades. Calefaction is a mana-efficiency downgrade despite being higher damage per cast.

stacking.notes: Instant direct damage - no buff slots involved.

members.name: Searing Arrow
members.note: Post-classic Ranger line (Luclin era). Not present on P99.

members.name: Flaming Arrow
members.note: Live EQ: Ranger 29, 113 damage instant (Allakhazam spell 3565). Legends: 102 up-front + 51/tick.

members.name: Burning Arrow
members.note: Live EQ: Ranger 39, 182 damage. Legends: 155 + 78/tick.

members.name: Scorching Arrow
members.note: Legends: 210 + 105/tick.

replacement.note: Monotonic damage; each replaces the previous. On Legends every member is a hybrid nuke + 6-second DoT, which is a Legends re-shape - the live-EQ versions are pure instant nukes.

stacking.notes: The 6-second DoT component means two arrow casts in quick succession may overwrite each other's DoT tick - unverified on Legends.

lines.name: Lightning nuke line

members.name: Invoke Lightning
members.note: Classic Druid 5 / Ranger 15. Targeted AE.

members.name: Careless Lightning
members.note: Classic Druid 19 / Ranger 39. Single target.

replacement.note: Careless Lightning does far more damage but is single-target; Invoke Lightning is a Targeted AE. Different tools, not a clean replacement.

missingOnLegends: Fury of Air / Cascade of Hail (Druid-only)

lines.name: Flame Lick line (fire DoT + AC debuff)

members.name: Flame Lick
members.note: Classic Druid 1 / Ranger 9. -3 AC plus a small fire DoT. Requires a Fire Beetle Eye. Legends scales the DoT to 17/tick at L32 vs classic 3/tick.

members.name: Immolate
members.note: Classic Druid 29 / Ranger 49. -10 to -18 AC plus a large fire DoT. Legends 42-67/tick vs classic 24/tick.

replacement.note: Immolate is stronger on both the DoT and the AC debuff. Same effect family, so the later overwrites the earlier on a target.

conflicts.detail: The AC-reduction component shares a debuff slot with other AC debuffs; a stronger AC debuff on the same mob replaces a weaker one. Both members of this line carry it, so Flame Lick on an Immolated mob is a downgrade.

stacksWith.detail: Insect-swarm DoTs are a separate DoT and run concurrently with Flame Lick / Immolate.

stacking.notes: This is the Ranger's only debuff line.

members.name: Stinging Swarm
members.note: Classic Druid 14 / Ranger 30. Legends 27-42/tick vs classic 13/tick.

members.name: Swarm of Pain
members.note: Post-classic - not on the P99 Ranger or Druid lists. 50-56/tick on Legends.

members.name: Drones of Doom
members.note: Classic Druid 34 / Ranger 54. Legends 148-156/tick vs classic 34/tick.

replacement.note: Monotonic damage; same DoT family so the later member overwrites the earlier on a target.

conflicts.detail: Members of this line overwrite each other on a target; a second Ranger casting a lower member wipes the higher one.

stacksWith.detail: Different DoT family - Immolate and Drones of Doom run together.

stacking.notes: These DoTs draw aggro on landing and each tick; the classic Ranger root-rot pattern is root + Immolate + Drones.

members.name: Ward Summoned
members.note: Classic Druid 5 / Ranger 22.

members.name: Dismiss Summoned
members.note: Classic Druid 24 / Ranger 39.

replacement.note: Straight damage upgrade against Construct/Elemental targets.

stacking.notes: Rangers stop at Dismiss Summoned in classic; the higher members are Druid-only, so the Legends omission is correct, not a gap.

members.name: Jolt
members.note: Classic Ranger 55 (Kunark). -500 hate, magic resist check.

members.name: Cinder Jolt
members.note: Classic Ranger 55 (Velious). -500 hate, FIRE resist check.

replacement.note: Sidegrade, not an upgrade: identical -500 hate, but Cinder Jolt is checked against fire resist instead of magic resist. Keep both and pick by the mob's resistances.

stacking.notes: Instant hate reduction, no buff slot.

members.name: Cancel Magic
members.note: Classic Druid 19 / Ranger 30. Cancel Magic (1) - one dispel attempt.

replacement.note: Nullify Magic is the strict upgrade (4 dispel attempts) but is absent from the Legends file.

stacking.notes: MISSING ON LEGENDS: Nullify Magic is a classic Ranger 58 spell (P99 Ranger/Spells, Kunark era; also Druid 44). Its absence leaves the Legends Ranger with only single-attempt dispel at level 60.

members.name: Invigor
members.note: Classic Druid 14 / Ranger 30. -35 stamina loss.

members.name: Extinguish Fatigue
members.note: Classic Druid 29 / Ranger 52. -90 stamina loss.

replacement.note: Larger stamina recovery; same effect.

stacking.notes: Effectively obsolete once stamina stopped gating melee, but classic-accurate.

standalone.name: Glimpse
standalone.note: Classic Ranger 9. Self-only +55% magnification (zoom). No upgrade exists; Bind Sight is a different effect.

standalone.name: Dance of the Fireflies
standalone.note: Classic Ranger 15. Summons a light source (Firefly Globe). Also Druid 1. No upgrade line for Rangers.

standalone.name: Hawk Eye
standalone.note: +10% chance to hit, self, permanent. NOT in the classic P99 Ranger list and not a Druid spell - Legends-specific (or post-classic). No upgrade found. Effect is unlike anything on the P99 Buff Lines page, so stacking is unknown.

standalone.name: Cure Poison
standalone.note: Classic Ranger 15. -4 poison counters. The upgrade (Counteract Poison, Druid 29) is Druid-only, so this is correctly a single spell for Rangers.

standalone.name: Panic Animal
standalone.note: Classic Ranger 22. Animal-only fear. The upgrade (Terrorize Animal, Druid 19) is Druid-only.

standalone.name: Bind Sight
standalone.note: Classic Ranger 22. See through the target's eyes. Ranger/Druid scouting utility, no upgrade.

standalone.name: Enduring Breath
standalone.note: Classic Ranger 22. Water breathing, consumes Fish Scales. No Ranger upgrade.

standalone.name: Cure Disease
standalone.note: -4 disease counters. NOT on the P99 classic Ranger list (Rangers get only Cure Poison in classic); it is Druid 5. Legends grants it to Rangers.

standalone.name: See Invisible
standalone.note: NOT on the P99 classic Ranger list; it is Druid 14. Legends grants it to Rangers.

standalone.name: Levitate
standalone.note: Classic Ranger 39. Consumes a Bat Wing. Levitation is its own effect and overwrites other levitate sources.

standalone.name: Call of Flame
standalone.note: Classic Ranger 49, obtained from the Call of Flame Quest rather than a vendor. A one-off fire nuke (300 on Legends) that sits between Ignite and Firestrike in the fire-DD progression but upgrades nothing and is upgraded by nothing.

unlinked.info: MISSING ON LEGENDS - Chloroplast. Classic Ranger 55 (also Druid 44, Shaman 39): +10 HP/tick regeneration, HP-Regeneration slot 1. Its absence means the Legends Ranger has NO regeneration buff at all except the incidental +2/tick rider on Skin Like Nature (which is regen slot 4, not slot 1). This is the single largest capability gap versus the classic Ranger.
MISSING ON LEGENDS - Nullify Magic. Classic Ranger 58 (Kunark), Cancel Magic (4). Leaves the Legends Ranger with only the level-30 single-attempt Cancel Magic.

HP-Regeneration slot 1 (Chloroplast, Regeneration, Regrowth, Regrowth of the Grove, Fungal Regrowth) is a separate heading from HP-Regeneration slot 4 (Skin Like Nature's +2, Natureskin's +4, the Rejuvenation potions). So a Fungi Staff or a druid's Regrowth stacks with Skin Like Nature's regen rider, but a Rejuvenation potion does not.

P99 internal inconsistency worth recording: the Ranger/Spells page omits Spikecoat from its level 49 block, but the Buff Lines page lists 'Spikecoat (Self-only: Druid 39, Ranger 49)' in both AC slot 2 and Damage Shield slot 3. Spikecoat IS a classic Ranger spell; Legends has it at 42.
P99 internal inconsistency: Endure Cold and Resist Cold are listed as Ranger 22 and Ranger 55 (Velious era) on Ranger/Spells but as Ranger 9 and Ranger 49 on Buff Lines. Legends uses 18 and 55.

Classic applies a hybrid-class penalty to some Ranger casts - P99 records Greater Healing as '288 (L24) to 300 (L30) (Hybrid Classes: 244 to 270 HP)'. This is the most likely explanation for the paired Skin-line rows in the Legends file, where one row carries lower AC than the other.
Rangers have no haste spell in any era, so the shaman/enchanter Haste (Primary) line and the Ervaj/v2 line never conflict with anything a Ranger casts.

Aegolism (Cleric 60) is the only buff that occupies AC slot 1 AND slot 4 simultaneously; it therefore blocks the Ranger's Skin line and the cleric Aegis line at once, and per the P99 max-HP table it is a net -70 HP versus the best mixed stack. A Ranger being buffed by a full cleric should prefer Heroism + Aegis + Symbol over Aegolism where the choice exists.

openQuestions: Every Skin-line spell appears TWICE in the Legends file - once with 'Increase Armor Class by N' (lower AC, level equal or 1-2 lower, targetType 'Single Friendly (or Self)') and once with 'Increase AC by N' (exactly the classic P99 values and the classic Ranger level, targetType 'Single'). Are these two distinct castable spells on Legends, a hybrid-penalty variant pair, or duplicated DB rows that should be de-duplicated before display? Same question for the AC phrasing on Riftwind's Protection, the coat line and Call of Earth.

Legends' Riftwind's Protection grants +30 AC while the level-48 Call of Earth grants only +20 AC (live EQ has 11-12 and 24-25 respectively). Is the +30 intentional, and does Call of Earth actually overwrite it in-game? If it does, the level-48 spell is an AC downgrade.

Force of Nature (L50) grants +5 damage shield and +6 HP/tick - which damage-shield slot and which regen slot? If its DS is slot 1 it conflicts with Shield of Spikes; if slot 3 it conflicts with the coat line. If its regen is slot 1 it partly replaces the missing Chloroplast.

Does casting Strength of Nature's 'Block new spell if slot 4 is effect Max Hitpoints and < 400' fire on Legends? If so, Rangers must be told to accept cleric/Skin HP buffs BEFORE self-casting Strength of Nature.
Do Spirit of the Shrew / Pack Shrew's Ultravision and Chill Sight's Ultravision overwrite each other on Legends?
Are added-melee-proc buffs (Call of Sky, Call of Fire) mutually exclusive with each other and with other proc buffs on Legends? No classic-source table covers proc buffs.
Legends' Ensnare is the same -40% as Snare (duration upgrade only). Intentional re-tier or a data error?

Our wiki mirror anchors a 'Blessing of the Page line' and a 'Shielding line'. Neither appears on the P99 AC/HP tables under those names (Shielding maps to the caster AC-slot-2 / HP-Shielding-Talisman entries). Confirm against the mirror whether Blessing of the Page shares a slot with the Skin line before publishing Ranger stacking advice.

Four spells in the file have no classic-era counterpart at all and should be confirmed as Legends-authored rather than mis-transcribed: Tangling Weeds, Hawk Eye, Harmony of Nature, Swarm of Pain (plus Nature's Precision and Force of Nature, which are named like later-era live spells).
